flags.message: 1 statutory approval(s) are modelled as starting at project start and running their typical duration. The library records how long an approval takes but not when it is lodged, so an approval binds only where its duration outlasts the work it gates. Approvals late in the programme are therefore modelled as non-binding, which understates their risk.
39 assembled activities rest on 7 unverified library entries; their confidence is the capped value, not the reasoner's claim.

nodes.answer: Build dedicated substation - HT substation is on our scope
nodes.label: What is the grid position: is a dedicated substation being built, or is the site feeder-ready?
nodes.why_stuck: Building a substation adds a long statutory and construction path ahead of energisation; a feeder-ready site does not. This shifts the critical path and the entire long-lead strategy, so the electrical sequence cannot be laid out until it is known.

nodes.answer: Not confirmed - use library estimate and flag
nodes.impact: Procurement placement and the critical path
nodes.label: Is the assumed lead time for this long-lead package confirmed by a vendor quotation or purchase order?
options: Not confirmed - use library estimate and flag
nodes.why_stuck: Lead time on the long-lead gear usually drives RFS. Guessing it is dangerous because the whole programme is built on it, and an unconfirmed guess looks identical to a confirmed date once it is in the plan.

nodes.answer: Owner-furnished under the client Cummins framework
nodes.impact: Delivery milestone as constraint vs procurement fragnet
nodes.label: Which equipment packages are owner-furnished, and which are contractor-supplied?
nodes.why_stuck: It changes who controls the delivery dates. Owner-furnished gear enters the plan as a delivery milestone constraint outside the contractor's control; contractor-supplied gear expands into a procurement fragnet the contractor owns. Getting this wrong misplaces the critical path.

nodes.answer: N+1 confirmed on electrical and cooling
nodes.label: What is the confirmed redundancy topology (N+1, 2N, 2N+1) for the power and cooling trains?
nodes.why_stuck: Redundancy drives equipment counts and the sequencing logic. N+1 and 2N produce materially different plant counts and different concurrent-maintainability constraints, so the equipment schedule and the commissioning structure cannot be derived until it is fixed.

provenance.note: Indian domestic transformer manufacturing is comparatively strong (CG Power, Bharat Bijlee, TBEA, Toshiba T&D), so 33/11kV units run shorter than the 40-60 week figure often quoted for Western markets. provenance.note: Authority and approval type from docs/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md#5. DURATION IS AN ESTIMATE. PESO licence for bulk HSD storage serving the generators; layout approval then licence. BLOCKS NARROWED FOR REVIEW: was ["commissioning"], which held the entire commissioning stage behind a diesel-storage licence and so gated L1 factory acceptance testing. A PESO licence covers bulk HSD storage and the fuel system, so it now blocks "genset_fuel_systems" - the generator installation and the bulk storage tank. This is a DATA CORRECTION and wants a compliance reviewer to confirm it. The open question was whether PESO should also gate the L5 integrated systems test, which runs the gensets under load on stored diesel. RESOLVED: no, and deliberately. The licence covers STORING petroleum, not testing on it, so listing the IST here would misstate its scope in compliance data. The constraint reaches the IST anyway - PESO gates the bulk storage, the storage gates energisation, and commissioning follows the power train - so a direct edge would change no date and add no governance: the IST is already Tier-1 and export-blocking through safety.ist_under_load. The reason to want the direct edge was that a future reorder of the power train could silently drop the chain; that is answered by test_the_ist_stays_downstream_of_the_diesel_licence, which fails if the transitive path is ever broken, rather than by a redundant link in the exported programme.
